title: 05_severe_phase_portrait_co_svr
interpretation: Severe sepsis (severity 3) plotted as a path in cardiac-output x vascular-resistance space rather than as two separate time series. Dots mark 6-hour intervals; the square is the shared healthy baseline (t=0), the stars are the 48 h endpoints, and grey dashes are iso-MAP contours (MAP = 17.34 x CO x SVR — a relation that holds to <0.5% in BOTH arms with the same constant). Both arms begin at the same point and finish on nearly the same low-MAP contour (~72 vs ~70 mmHg), but by orthogonal routes: the real BioGears engine slides LEFT — cardiac output fails 5.8->4.5 L/min while SVR stays flat (cold, low-output shock) — whereas the SBML extraction slides DOWN — it holds/rebuilds output and lets SVR swing up then collapse to 0.67 (warm, vasodilatory shock). The orthogonality is the finding: the extraction's single AIR->sympathetic arc overshoots the vasomotor axis that the engine's full cardiovascular control keeps muted, so the two reach the same MAP by physiologically different shock states. This is the geometric view of studies 03/05.
